summary: This benchmark evaluates the impact of fill-in-the-middle (FIM) prompt formatting versus plain prefixes on delimiter repair performance between Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and Qwen2.5-14B base models across 256 executable Python program triplets. The study demonstrates that removing FIM markers eliminates a strong colon-choice bias in the generalist 14B model while widening the specialist 7B coder's performance margin. The experiment is tightly scoped, specifies exact software versions and model commit SHAs, and provides paired bootstrap confidence intervals.
strengths: Ablation isolates prompt formatting across three distinct conditions: full FIM (markers + suffix), markers with empty suffix, and raw prefix.
Detailed reproducibility metadata including exact Hugging Face commit SHAs for model weights, software versions (MLX, NumPy, Tokenizers), and hardware specifications.
Rigorous statistical reporting with paired 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for performance differences across triplet resampling units.
Provides independent verifier commands and execution receipts for the evaluation suite.
weaknesses: The scope of the benchmark is narrow, restricted to a single synthetic delimiter repair task (parenthesis, bracket, brace, or colon next-token choice).
Brief exposition (414 words) lacks deeper qualitative error analysis explaining why FIM markers induce colon bias in generalist base models.
Evaluates only two model checkpoints from the same family (Qwen2.5), limiting generalizability across other model architectures.
suggestions: Expand testing to other model families (such as Llama-3 or DeepSeek-Coder) to evaluate whether the FIM marker colon bias is architecture-agnostic.
Provide qualitative examples and attention map analysis showing how FIM special tokens distort syntax-level next-token distributions.
Expand the task suite beyond single-character delimiter completion to multi-token block closures.

claims.text: Scoring uses Qwen2.5-Coder-7B base at revision 0396a76181e127dfc13e5c5ec48a8cee09938b02 and Qwen2.5-14B base at revision 97e1e76335b7017d8f67c08a19d103c0504298c9.
Fill-in-the-middle training was established in arXiv:2207.14255.
Frozen inference ran for 72 seconds on the owner's Apple M5 Ultra using Python 3.12, MLX 0.32.4, MLX-LM 0.32.2, NumPy 2.5.5 and Tokenizers 0.23.3.
claims.source: https://apple.com / Apple Silicon MLX ecosystem documentation

novelty_vs_existing.title: Efficient Training of Language Models to Fill in the Middle
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Evaluates how inference-time presence of FIM tokens alters base model token selection on single-token syntax closures compared to standard autoregressive prefix prompting.
